name: Woodwork
intro: Explore materials, craftsmanship and responsible manufacture. BGE projects are suggestions only. Woodwork learning at home should focus on drawings, material choices and evaluation: tools, machines, finishes and practical making require teacher direction and school workshop safety procedures. National 4 and National 5 Practical Woodworking are genuine routes; there is no Higher Practical Woodworking.

bge.title: Wood as a material
bge.question: Why choose one timber over another?
bge.task: Create a comparison card for two timbers using appearance, workability and intended use.
bge.extend: Explain why hardwood does not mean every hardwood is physically harder than every softwood.

bge.title: Precision from a plan
bge.question: How does accuracy begin before cutting?
bge.task: Annotate a supplied drawing with a sequence of checks before any teacher-directed making.
bge.extend: Explain why repeated measuring from a reliable datum can reduce accumulated error.

bge.title: Joining ideas
bge.question: What makes a joint suitable?
learn: Relate joint choice to load and appearance.
bge.task: Compare two illustrated joints for a small frame and justify a choice without making it at home.
bge.extend: Identify a trade-off between appearance, strength and ease of manufacture.

bge.title: Design for long life
bge.question: Can a product be repaired?
bge.task: Evaluate a wooden school object from photographs: identify one repair or maintenance opportunity.
bge.extend: Produce a paper cutting layout that reduces offcuts.

senior.title: National 4 Practical Woodworking
areas: Making a Finished Product — added value
senior.explain: Develop practical skills, knowledge of materials and safe working with supervision.
senior.assessment: Internally assessed units and added-value practical activity; pass/fail.

senior.title: National 5 Practical Woodworking
senior.explain: Apply accurate marking out, manufacture, assembly and finishing with knowledge of tools and materials.
senior.assessment: The question paper was removed from session 2025–26. Current assessment is the practical activity, including a case study; use the current specification.

senior.title: Higher Design and Manufacture
senior.explain: A possible related progression where offered, rather than a Higher Woodworking qualification. It adds substantial design and analytical work.
senior.assessment: A distinct qualification with its own question paper and assignment requirements. Discuss readiness and school availability.

skills.title: Read a working drawing
skills.explain: Identify overall and component dimensions before choosing a sequence.
skills.try: Highlight the thickness, width and length of one component.
skills.check: Units and real dimensions are clear; do not measure a screen image as though it were full size.

skills.title: Plan accurate work
skills.explain: Reference surfaces and planned checks support consistent results.
skills.try: Write a checking sequence for a fictional frame before assembly.
skills.check: Check dimensions, squareness and matching components before irreversible work.

skills.title: Explain a joint
skills.explain: A joint choice should suit the product and direction of loading.
skills.try: Annotate where two components meet in a supplied drawing.
skills.check: State why the selected joint fits the task, not merely its name.

skills.title: Evaluate workmanship
skills.explain: Use evidence such as fit, alignment, finish and compliance with dimensions.
skills.try: Write a specific evaluation of a teacher-provided sample photograph.
skills.check: Separate what is visible from what would need physical measurement.

practice.question: A frame drawing specifies two rails of 240 mm and two of 180 mm. Is 840 mm timber necessarily enough?
practice.hint: Think beyond the sum of the finished parts.
practice.answer: The finished lengths total 840 mm, but cutting allowance, defects, joint requirements and stock preparation may require more. Confirm the cutting list and teacher-approved plan before manufacture.
practice.extend: Sketch a stock layout including a stated cutting allowance.

practice.question: Why should a component be checked for squareness before final assembly?
practice.hint: Consider consequences of an early error.
practice.answer: An out-of-square component can distort the assembly, create gaps and prevent correct fitting. Checking before final assembly allows correction at a stage when it may still be practical.
practice.extend: Identify two other checks needed before assembly.

practice.question: A polished surface looks attractive. Does this prove a product is well made?
practice.answer: No. Check dimensions, joint fit, stability, suitability for use and finish quality. A good-looking surface may hide weak joints or inaccurate components.
practice.extend: Create a balanced evaluation checklist with measurable criteria.

ipad.title: Plan annotation
steps: Record a short explanation of the assembly order.
ipad.evidence: A plan that communicates understanding before practical work.

ipad.title: Craftsmanship record
steps: With permission, photograph only your own school workshop work at safe checkpoints.
Annotate a measurement or quality check.
Explain one improvement before the next supervised stage.
ipad.evidence: A private process record without classmates or personal information.

ipad.title: Material choice board
steps: Collect permitted images of two timber options.
Write a justified recommendation for a brief.
ipad.evidence: A sourced design decision, not an unsupervised making task.

parentTip: Discuss a drawing or material choice at home. Practical workshop tasks must remain teacher-directed; do not encourage pupils to recreate tool or machine operations independently.
